page: Amazon Web Services r8i.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores of a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in multi-core processing and memory operations. The server achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 21093.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 82754.83, both placing in the top tier and strong categories respectively. Memory bandwidth tests showed a strong read-only small block cached speed of 5123.16 GB/sec and a large block uncached speed of 192.43 GB/sec, though the large block write speed of 76.62 GB/sec was average. The CPU's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), contribute to strong performance in specialized tasks, such as a Passmark CPU extended instructions score of 88554.97 and a Redis SET throughput of 120.37 million operations per second.

Given its high memory density of 512.0 GB and strong multi-core performance, the r8i.16xlarge is configured for memory-intensive workloads. It is suitable for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks. For example, LLM inference tests using a 7B model achieved 296.71 tokens per second for prompt processing. The absence of local storage and GPUs represents a tradeoff, making it less suitable for local disk-heavy I/O or GPU-accelerated deep learning, but highly cost-efficient for memory-bound enterprise applications that utilize network storage.

It features 512.0 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. Benchmark results show top-tier performance in multi-core processing, software compilation, and Redis operations, alongside strong memory read bandwidth. However, memory write speeds for large blocks remain average. With hardware-accelerated instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX, this instance is highly efficient for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory databases, large-scale caching, and text processing, offering a balanced tradeoff between high memory capacity and dedicated compute power without local storage overhead.
